name: app_routines
description: Manage this bot's persistent routines directly. Operations: list; create kind=once with at (ISO-8601 seconds and explicit offset/Z), or kind=recurring with cron (5 fields), or kind=watch with cron and command (the app runs that shell command in this bot's folder on the schedule without waking you, and wakes you only when it exits non-zero, times out or prints a line starting with ALERT; task is its name). create requires task and unique request_id (reuse on retries), optional timezone (IANA, defaults to local at creation). Returns saved id/status; use id for pause/resume/cancel. List includes legacy cron IDs. Reschedule by cancel then create with a new request_id. Once jobs overdue while closed run on next app check; recurring catches up only today in its saved timezone. fired means the trigger reached the app router, not proof of agent startup or task completion. delivery_uncertain means a crash may have interrupted dispatch: never auto retry. Cancel stops future dispatch, not active work. App must be running; no OS wakeup. Do not edit app-owned schedule JSON or use shell/cron for this tool.

name: app_monitor_start
description: Coordinator only; workers must return command intent in their task report. Start one already authorized command in this bot workspace after an explicit Allow once card, including in auto mode. Supply command as shell text. This is a completion monitor, not a polling/line-event monitor. Returns monitor_id and awaitingApproval immediately; finish the turn without polling. The app queues app_monitor_result on success or nonzero failure with monitor_id, owner_session_id, exit_code and bounded output. No network or permission escalation. Never use to expand scope, bypass a denial or rerun interrupted work. Stop/cancel suppresses callbacks. Commands are not replayed on restart; unconfirmed executions become interrupted. Callback dispatch interrupted before acknowledgement is uncertain and never automatically duplicated; inspect status/owner thread.

name: app_monitor_status
description: Get one monitor by monitor_id, or list this owner session’s monitors when omitted. Includes execution result and wake delivery state; no external PID adoption.

name: app_monitor_cancel
description: Cancel one owned monitor and suppress any queued completion wake. Cancellation is best effort; side effects cannot be undone. A finished command keeps its actual exit status.

name: app_handoff
description: Assign one independently accepted deliverable to an app-managed worker. Returns acceptance and task_id immediately, not a completed result. Continue other independent, authorized handoffs and required report decisions in the current dispatch phase, then finish the turn without waiting. The app delivers correlated app_task_result reports in later turns. A new handoff does not resolve the active report. Optional effort sets the worker's reasoning effort (low, medium, high, xhigh; default: the Codex workers setting, else yours). Optional model runs the worker on a Codex model Codex offers, by slug (e.g. gpt-6-luna) or short name (e.g. luna); default: the Codex workers setting, else yours. Workers are always Codex; model picks only which Codex model.

group.description: The job this worker is for, a short name (e.g. "Compare GPU clouds"). Give every worker you start for the same job the same group, so the app lists them as one job.

role.description: Only for the plugin-library Maintainer: launch its existing Claude ccb-core component editor on its configured model. No new folders, tools, authorization or settings. Omit for ordinary work.

isolated_git.description: Optional explicit authorization for an implementation task only. Enables single-request automatic approval of creation of a NEW isolated bot/ worktree, staging these exact task-owned files and commits on that branch. repo must equal this bot workspace root; baseCommit is an existing full commit SHA. worktree must be a new direct child /private/tmp/botling-2x-* or /Volumes/My-SSD/botling-work/<name>. Unknown/invalid ownership falls back to manual approval. Never use for research-only tasks. Any app_send_message revokes this grant; push/merge/deletion/shared checkout and shell chains always retain normal approval.

name: app_send_message
description: Send a follow-up within the same worker task/session; never append a new independent deliverable. Busy workers receive steering; idle workers start a new turn. Returns acceptance, not the completed result. Continue other eligible dispatches and required report decisions before ending the dispatch phase. Only continuation of the active report task_id resolves that report.

name: app_task_checkpoint
description: Resolve the active app_task_result against the authorized user objective. Worker completed means only its execution turn ended. Record concrete acceptance evidence, an exact user input/permission needed, a real blocker, or an actively running dependency. Continue the same authorized task with app_send_message when needed. A new handoff or a message to another task does not resolve this report; after dispatching a separate downstream worker, explicitly record waiting_dependency with its task_id. A bare waiting status is not completion. This checkpoint grants no new authorization.

name: app_browser_tabs
description: List the tabs open in the user's in-app browser pane beside your chat: tab_id, url, title, which one is selected, and how many network requests were captured. The pane is the user's own browser (their sign-ins); you read it, you do not drive it.

name: app_browser_open
description: Open an http(s) address in a tab of the user's browser pane beside your chat (it shows the pane; an open tab on that address is selected instead). Its network traffic is captured from then on, for app_browser_requests. Returns tab_id; the page loads in the background.

name: app_browser_requests
description: Read the network requests a tab of the user's browser pane made (captured in the background since the tab opened, the latest 500): method, URL, type, status, request and response headers, post data, and response bodies with include_bodies. Filter with url_contains, resource_type, method, limit. Cookie, Set-Cookie and Authorization are masked unless unmasked_headers. Use it to find a site's API and build a tool on it. save_as json saves everything to a file.

tab_id.description: A tab of your browser pane, from app_browser_tabs (e.g. t3). Default: the tab the user has selected.

url_contains.description: Only requests whose URL contains this text (case does not matter).

resource_type.description: Only this DevTools resource type: document, xhr (Fetch/XHR), script, stylesheet, image, font, media, websocket, other.

limit.description: The newest this many matching requests (default 50).

include_bodies.description: Include response bodies (text; base64 for binary). Default false.

unmasked_headers.description: Show Cookie, Set-Cookie and Authorization values instead of <masked>. Only when the user asked for them.

save_as.description: Save the full result to a file (csv: rows or the first table) and get its path; give the user that path as a link in your reply. Large results are saved anyway.

name: app_browser_extract
description: Read data from the page in a tab of the user's browser pane: its tables, visible text, links, the elements matching a CSS selector, or your own read-only script's result (JSON). Nothing on the page is clicked, typed or submitted. Data the user should get (a table, a CSV) goes to a file with save_as; link that file in your reply.

tab_id.description: A tab of your browser pane, from app_browser_tabs (e.g. t3). Default: the tab the user has selected.

what.description: tables: every <table> as headers + rows (default); text: the page's visible text; links: every link; selector: the elements matching selector; script: your own read-only script.

script.description: what: script. The body of an async function run in the page (an isolated world, sees the DOM): return JSON-able data, e.g. return [...document.querySelectorAll('.price')].map(e => e.textContent). Read-only: clicking, submitting, typing, navigation and network calls are refused.

save_as.description: Save the full result to a file (csv: rows or the first table) and get its path; give the user that path as a link in your reply. Large results are saved anyway.
